hints: Resolve perpendicular to the plane to find the normal reaction: $R = mg\cos 60^\circ$.
Since the block is on the point of slipping down the plane, limiting friction $F = \mu R$ acts up the plane.
Resolve forces parallel to the plane: $mg\sin 60^\circ = 15 + F$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the plane in equilibrium:
$$R = mg\cos 60^\circ = 3(10)(0.5) = 15\text{ N}$$
Since the block tends to slip down the plane, the limiting frictional force $F = \mu R = 15\mu$ acts up the plane.

Resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane in equilibrium:
$$mg\sin 60^\circ - 15 - F = 0$$
$$3(10)\sin 60^\circ - 15 - 15\mu = 0$$
$$30\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) - 15 - 15\mu = 0$$
$$15\sqrt{3} - 15 = 15\mu$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the perpendicular equilibrium equation for the block on the $60^\circ$ incline:
$$\Sigma F_\perp = 0 \implies R - mg\cos 60^\circ = 0$$
Substitute $m = 3\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R = 3 \times 10 \times \cos 60^\circ = 30 \times 0.5 = 15\text{ N}$$

Identify the direction and magnitude of the frictional force:
The block is on the point of slipping down the plane, so friction opposes this downward tendency and acts up the slope. In limiting equilibrium:
$$F = \mu R = 15\mu$$

State the parallel equilibrium equation along the incline (taking down-slope as positive):
$$\Sigma F_\parallel = 0 \implies mg\sin 60^\circ - 15 - F = 0$$
$$3 \times 10 \times \sin 60^\circ - 15 - 15\mu = 0$$
Substitute $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:
$$30 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - 15 - 15\mu = 0$$
$$15\sqrt{3} - 15 = 15\mu$$

Divide both sides by $15$:
$$\mu = \sqrt{3} - 1$$
Evaluating numerically:
$$\mu \approx 1.73205 - 1 = 0.73205$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $\mu = 0.732$ (or exact value $\sqrt{3} - 1$).

ai_rubric.Using Limiting Equilibrium: Sets $R = 15\text{ N}$, resolves along plane $30\sin 60^\circ - 15 - 15\mu = 0$, and solves for $\mu = 0.732$ (or $\sqrt{3} - 1$).
ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Correctly resolves weight components along and perpendicular to the inclined plane.

hints: For the greatest value of $X$, the block is on the point of slipping up the plane.
Therefore, limiting friction $F = \mu R = 15(\sqrt{3}-1)$ acts down the plane.
Resolve parallel to the plane: $X = mg\sin 60^\circ + F$.
walkthrough:
For the greatest force $X$ to prevent motion, the block is on the verge of slipping upwards, so limiting friction acts downwards along the slope:
$$F = \mu R = (\sqrt{3} - 1)(15) = 15\sqrt{3} - 15\text{ N} \approx 10.98\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces parallel to the plane in limiting equilibrium:
$$X - mg\sin 60^\circ - F = 0$$
$$X = 3(10)\sin 60^\circ + F = 15\sqrt{3} + (15\sqrt{3} - 15)$$
$$X = 30\sqrt{3} - 15 = 15(2\sqrt{3} - 1) \approx 51.9615 - 15 = 36.96\text{ N} \approx 37.0\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Analyze the limiting condition for maximum force $X$:
If $X$ is increased to its maximum value before motion occurs, the block tends to slip up the plane. Consequently, the limiting frictional force acts down the incline, resisting upward movement.

Calculate the forces opposing upward motion:
- Downward component of weight:
$$mg\sin 60^\circ = 3 \times 10 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 15\sqrt{3}\text{ N} \approx 25.9808\text{ N}$$
- Limiting friction acting downwards:
$$F = \mu R = (\sqrt{3} - 1) \times 15 = 15\sqrt{3} - 15 \approx 10.9808\text{ N}$$

Formulate the equilibrium equation along the incline:
$$X - mg\sin 60^\circ - F = 0$$
$$X = mg\sin 60^\circ + F$$
$$X = 15\sqrt{3} + (15\sqrt{3} - 15) = 30\sqrt{3} - 15$$
$$X = 15(2\sqrt{3} - 1)$$
Evaluate numerically:
$$X \approx 30(1.73205) - 15 = 51.9615 - 15 = 36.9615\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $X = 37.0\text{ N}$ (or exact form $15(2\sqrt{3} - 1)\text{ N}$).

ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Sets $X = 30\sin 60^\circ + F$ and calculates $X = 37.0\text{ N}$ (or $15(2\sqrt{3} - 1)\text{ N}$).
